title: introduce-multiresolution-latency-shingling-and-dynamic-alert-weighting
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: We see frequent noisy alerts driven by short-lived high-latency tokens and bursty invocation patterns that skew percentile-based SLOs. This PR introduces a multiresolution 'latency shingling' index to capture short, medium, and long-window latency distributions per-route and per-tenant, and a dynamic alert-weighting layer that reduces noise by down-weighting transient microbursts while preserving sensitivity to sustained regressions. Motivation: current percentile rollups are single-resolution and overly sensitive to bursty tails; investigating incidents shows many pages were caused by transient caches/kv-warmups rather than real regressions. Changes in this PR: - Add invocation-level shingle key generation (invocation_shingle_key) in the runtime telemetry pipeline; key is derived from route+model+cohort and a time bucket. - Emit three concurrent latency histograms (shingle_1s, shingle_30s, shingle_10m) per invocation for short/medium/long windows; histograms are compacted into rollups in the ingest tier. - Introduce Alert Weighting Service: a small scoring service that computes a weight for each alerting signal based on recent shingle stability, tenant burstiness, and a confidence score derived from sample counts. - Update alerting rules: existing route SLO alerts now multiply the raw signal by the computed weight and apply a minimum-confidence threshold. - Dashboard: new Grafana panels (Latency Shingle Viewer, Weighted Alert Heatmap, Burstiness Cohorts) and a per-tenant drill-down that visualizes weight history. - Backfill transformer: optional re-aggregation job to create shingle rollups from recent raw spans for customers who want historical baselines. - Tests and e2e: unit tests for key derivation, integration test injecting synthetic bursts, and a canary deployment in staging with 48h burn. Implementation notes: the shingling code is implemented in runtime/telemetry/shingle_generator.go and a lightweight compactor in ingest/rollups/shingle_compactor.py. Alert Weighting Service is in observability/alert-weighting and exposes a gRPC endpoint and a fallback HTTP cache for rule-eval timeouts. Safety: default rollout is off; feature flag obs.multires_shingle=false. We ship with conservative defaults: short-window weight decay is aggressive to avoid suppressing real regressions; long-window sensitivity remains high. Migration: no data schema breaking changes; new metrics names are additive. Checklist: - [x] Instrumentation in runtime - [x] Compactor and rollup worker - [x] Alert rule changes with feature flag - [x] Grafana dashboards + panel links - [x] Integration + canary pass Related: ENG-3421 (alert noise reduction), ENG-3499 (latency profiling sprint), SUP-1182 (customer incident RCA).

review_conversation: Connor Li (reviewer): Can we ensure the shingle keys are stable across restarts? Please add a deterministic salt migration note.
Aisha (author): Shingle keys are deterministic; added migration note and unit test that validates stability across a simulated restart by using deterministic shard hashing.
Miguel Ortega (reviewer): The alert-weighting service should expose metrics about suppressed alerts for debugging; add an exported gauge and an event log when weight < 0.2.
Aisha: Added observability counters (alerts_evaluated,total; alerts_suppressed_by_weight,total) and a debug event emitted to audit stream. Also added docs for interpreting the gauge.
Rhea Chandra (approver): Verified canary for 48h in staging, no regression; a couple nits on comments fixed. Approving.
QA (comment): Integration test failed on first run due to clock skew in the canary; rerun passed after fix to test harness.
Release manager (comment): Need a short operational playbook for oncall: how to disable weighting if it hides a real regression — added to docs and ops checklist.
release_notes: Add multiresolution latency shingling and dynamic alert weighting to reduce alert noise from transient bursts; dashboards and an optional backfill tool included. Feature gated behind obs.multires_shingle.
notes: Rollout: enable behind feature flag; recommend enabling in staging for 72h before production. Ops: if suppression hides a real regression, set obs.multires_shingle=false or adjust minimum-confidence to 0.0 to temporarily disable weighting.
